scenario.description: One-region synthetic service and closing-stock incidence allocation across a present cohort, a future cohort and an explicitly unassigned shared asset.

cohort_allocations.allocation_rule: explicit synthetic assignments; no automatic population-proportional imputation

invariants: service demand, served and unmet reconcile separately for water_m3, energy_kwh and food_kg
inherited stock allocation reconciles separately for water_m3, energy_kwh and food_kg
financial obligations never net against physical resource stocks or obligations
changing welfare discount rates changes only the derived discounted-service view
cohort splitting and reassignment preserve aggregate physical totals
future cohorts inherit the preceding closing state rather than a reset baseline
claim_ceiling: All values are synthetic and are not calibrated to any real population, catchment, infrastructure system or fiscal account.
The implementation validates allocation and reconciliation contracts; it does not infer who actually received services from aggregate source-ledger totals.
Cohort assignments are explicit assumptions and must not be interpreted as observed incidence.
The welfare discount view is normative sensitivity analysis and is not a physical accounting operation.
Financial and physical obligations remain distinct and are not combined into a universal fairness or sustainability score.
